messages:
noah: quick live-thread from the all-hands runtime Q&A: i have a couple of follow-ups about caching regressions noted in the roadmap slides. who owns the KV-cache correctness tests?

lina: cache team owns it (hi!). main tests are correctness (no stale payloads), consistency under failover, and perf (hit-rate vs miss-latency).

omar: were there any test failures during the last cache rollout? slides showed a small bump in 95/99.

lina: yes, one edge-case: multi-tenant key prefix collisions under short TTL led to a higher tail on cold starts. we patched the key namespace and added prefix-hashing.

noah: can we get the test vectors and the regression repro steps? want to share with a customer who's worried.

lina: posted on confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/cache/regressions/1984560000  includes traffic replay snippets and load scripts.

cory: on batching: is the plan to let the runtime auto-tune batch wait based on recent seq_len histograms? sounds dangerous for tail-sensitive apps.

omar: short answer: auto-tune is opt-in. default is fixed wait. auto-tune module will recommend values and can be enabled per-route.

noah: what about kernel work: are we still shipping kernel-quant-v2 Q2? all-hands slide seemed fuzzy.

lina: quant-v2 target slipped slightly; current plan: internal trials in Q2, public canary in early Q3. blockers: dequant perf regression on long sequences and some fp16 numerics for a small model set.

ci-bot: ci: kernel-quant-v2 branch has 2 failing tests (numerics) at 1984560101

omar: anything customers should expect to change when quant-v2 lands? memory footprint, cold-start times?

lina: expect ~2-2.5x memory reduction for large models, slightly faster cold-starts due to smaller kernels, but watch for small accuracy diffs on numeric-sensitive ops. we'll provide a compatibility matrix.

noah: perf-bot: any perf baselines for quant-v2 vs quant-v1?

perf-bot: perf-summary: quant-v2 internal bench shows median token latency -6% and p99 +4% on long sequences; short sequences p99 improved -10%. data from canary narrow machines.

cory: action items: lina publish regression repro + patch notes, marjoram schedule customer sync for the worried account, infra to earmark a canary cluster for quant-v2.

omar: i volunteered infra. will reserve cluster-canary-q2 and post schedule once provisioned.

noah: thanks all. small ask: can we get a simple one-pager for customers summarizing what to expect when kernels/quant change? lmk if product can draft.

lina: product please? ccing @cory for follow-up.

cory: on it, will draft and circulate in #docs.

noah: cool. reconvene in ~1h for any new canary updates.
